summary: Lists the requirements that a middlebox communication (midcom) protocol must satisfy so applications can influence middlebox behavior. The focus is on network address translators and firewalls. It states needs rather than defining the protocol itself.

eli5.summary: Before building a tool, you write down what it must do. This document is that checklist for a protocol that lets programs ask firewalls to open the right doors.

questions: what are the midcom protocol requirements
how do applications control nat and firewalls
subtitle: The checklist of what a protocol for talking to firewalls and NATs must be able to do.

tldr.problem: Applications sometimes need to influence middleboxes such as firewalls and network address translators, but no agreed protocol existed for it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists numbered requirements for a midcom protocol covering protocol machinery, semantics and security, derived from the midcom framework.
tldr.outcome: It states needs only; the protocol itself is defined elsewhere. The framework is in RFC 3303.

facts.label: Filter 5-tuple
facts.value: source and destination address and port, plus transport protocol

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This document is one of two from the Middlebox Communication (midcom) working group, addressing a protocol between middleboxes and midcom agents. This one gives the requirements, and the framework document (RFC 3303) gives the context, terminology and definitions, and should be read with it.

The requirements were extracted, both explicit and implicit, from the midcom framework. The focus is on network address translation and firewall middleboxes.
sections.eli5: A middlebox is a gatekeeper in the network. Midcom is how a program politely asks the gatekeeper for help.

sections.title: Protocol Machinery Requirements
sections.content:
The protocol must let an agent establish an authorized association with a middlebox, and the middlebox must be able to decide whether to permit it. An agent must be able to talk to more than one middlebox at once, and a middlebox to more than one agent. When many agents interact with one middlebox, overall behavior must be deterministic, avoiding race conditions.

The protocol must let the parties reach a known and stable state, including after power or other failure, so resources used by a failed element can be released. The middlebox must be able to report its status and send unsolicited messages about asynchronous conditions, such as closing pinholes after a resource shortage. Agent and middlebox must authenticate each other, either side may end the session, and an agent must be able to tell whether a request succeeded.

The protocol must include version interworking, which may include a protocol version number, and the behavior of overlapping rules must be predictable, for example by a known precedence.
sections.eli5: Both sides must prove who they are, be able to say goodbye, and always know whether a request worked.

sections.title: Protocol Semantics Requirements
sections.content:
The syntax and semantics must be extensible, for example to add new message types as more middlebox types are supported. An agent must be able to install a ruleset covering several action types, such as firewall and NAT, and to group rulesets so one message can tear down, extend or manipulate all of them. An agent must be able to extend the lifetime of a ruleset that would otherwise be deleted. Several authorized agents must not be precluded from working on the same ruleset.

If a peer does not understand an option, it must be clear whether to proceed without it or reject the request. Failure reasons must let agent behavior adapt, without making attacks easier.

Rules must be able to carry filters including the 5-tuple: source address, source port, destination address, destination port and transport protocol. When the middlebox maps ports, the protocol should let an agent ask for the external port to have the same oddity as the internal one and for a consecutive range of ports to map to consecutive internal ports, both to support RTP and RTCP. A more specific filter should be able to override an overlapping ruleset, for example to disallow a subset of allowed traffic.
sections.eli5: The checklist says the language must be able to grow, handle groups of rules, and say exactly what went wrong when a request fails.

sections.title: Security Requirements
sections.content:
The protocol must provide message authentication, confidentiality and integrity. Confidentiality protection of control messages must be optional, and if provided it should allow a choice of algorithm. The protocol must operate securely across untrusted domains and define mechanisms to mitigate replay attacks on control messages.

The Security Considerations section of the RFC simply refers to these requirements.
sections.eli5: Messages to the gatekeeper must be signed, not tampered with, and not replayable by a sneaky copier.
